paper_metadata.title: A Quantum Online Portfolio Optimization Algorithm

summary: The paper proposes a theoretical quantum online portfolio optimization algorithm with regret bound 12/r_min * sqrt(log(n)/(2T)) and runtime O~(T^3 sqrt(n/r_min) log^{1.5}(1/delta)). It compares against classical baselines with regret bounds 1/r_min * sqrt(log(n)/(2T)), 2/r_min * sqrt(log(n)/(2T)), and 8/r_min * sqrt(log(n)/(2T)), but reports no hardware experiments or empirical speedup.

experiments.description: Quantum online portfolio optimization algorithm for sequential portfolio selection using quantum state preparation, quantum inner product estimation, and quantum multi-sampling; evaluated theoretically against the classical online portfolio optimization baseline and its sampling/approximate variants.

algorithm.variant: Quantum online portfolio optimization algorithm (Algorithm 4) with quantum inner product estimation and quantum multi-sampling

hyperparameters.delta: failure probability parameter; theorem stated for delta in (0,1/3)
hyperparameters.s: number of samples per round (input parameter)
hyperparameters.r_min: known lower bound on price relatives

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Quantum access to price-relative vectors via oracles U_rho(t) acting on O(log n) qubits; portfolio weights represented implicitly through q(t) and normalized to w(t)=q(t)/||q(t)||_1
problem_formulation.objective_function: Online portfolio selection maximizing cumulative log wealth sum_t log(w(t)·rho(t)) with exponentiated-gradient style updates; regret measured against best fixed portfolio in hindsight
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: No short-selling constraint; portfolio weights are nonnegative and sum to 1; transaction cost C per invested asset; approximate updates use relative-error inner product and norm estimates

problem_instance.description: Sequential online portfolio optimization over T trading days and n assets with price-relative vectors revealed online

dataset_specification.description: No specific market dataset named; analysis is generic and theoretical

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Uses closing prices; defines day-to-day return and price relatives normalized by daily maximum return so that max_i rho_i(t)=1 and r_min <= rho_i(t) <= 1
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Theoretical regret and runtime analysis; no numerical experiments reported

implementation_details.classical_solver: Classical baseline is the Helmbold et al. online portfolio optimization algorithm and its sampling/approximate variants; no specific solver software named
implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: None beyond theoretical oracle access assumptions
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Compute regret bounds and success probabilities analytically

classical_baselines.method_name: Helmbold et al. online portfolio optimization algorithm (Algorithm 1)
Helmbold et al. online portfolio optimization algorithm (Algorithm 1)
Helmbold et al. online portfolio optimization algorithm (Algorithm 1)

speedup_claims.conditions: in terms of n, using quantum state preparation, quantum inner product estimation, and quantum multi-sampling; asymptotic runtime stated as O~(T^3 * sqrt(n / r_min) * log^{1.5}(1/delta)) versus O(T * n) for Algorithm 1
speedup_claims.caveats: The paper is theoretical only; no hardware experiment. The speedup is in n, but the overall runtime has strong T dependence and assumes quantum oracle/qRAM access.

speedup_claims.conditions: quantum multi-sampling replaces classical multi-sampling; compared against O(T^2 * n * log(T/delta)) classical runtime
speedup_claims.caveats: Still requires online oracle access to price relatives and does not report empirical benchmarking.

speedup_claims.conditions: quantum inner product estimation and quantum state preparation replace classical counterparts; compared against O(T * n + T^2 / r_min * log(T/delta))
speedup_claims.caveats: The claimed advantage is asymptotic and depends on the oracle model and qRAM assumptions.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: ~O(T^3 * sqrt(n / r_min) * polylog(1/delta)) (stated as O~(T^3 sqrt(n/r_min) log^{1.5}(1/delta)))
complexity_analysis.classical_complexity: O(T n) for Algorithm 1; O(T^2 n log(T/delta)) for sampling-based classical variant; O(T^2 n + T^2/r_min log(T/delta)) for approximate sampling-based variant

advantage_assessment.crossover_size: Not assessed from paper; no empirical crossover study reported
advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: Requires qRAM/online quantum access to price relatives, quantum state preparation, quantum inner product estimation, quantum norm estimation, and quantum multi-sampling; asymptotic runtime is O~(T^3 sqrt(n / r_min) log^{1.5}(1/delta))
limiting_factors: No hardware experiment or simulator benchmark is reported
Assumes online quantum oracle access / qRAM for price relatives
Quadratic speedup in n is offset by large T dependence and constant-factor overheads
No demonstrated practical runtime advantage over classical baselines

notes: This paper is theoretical and does not report an actual hardware run, simulator benchmark, circuit depth, gate counts, shots, or optimizer settings.
The quantum algorithm uses amplitude estimation/inner-product estimation plus quantum multi-sampling; no QAOA/VQE/Grover experiment is present.
Hardware is not specified because the work is algorithmic rather than experimental.
The paper explicitly presents a theoretical quantum algorithm and compares it analytically to classical baselines.
No experimental quantum advantage is demonstrated on hardware.
